title: US Sends Third Aircraft Carrier Toward Iran as November Buildup Escalates
excerpt: The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group departed San Diego on Sunday, bound for waters around Iran, as the Pentagon builds to three carriers and two amphibious groups in the region by the end of November.
body:
• A US official told Al Jazeera the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group departed San Diego on Sunday, bound for the waters around Iran, as the US-Iran war enters its eighth month.
  • By the end of November, three US aircraft carriers and two amphibious landing groups are expected to be positioned around Iran.
  • The new deployment adds thousands of troops and F-35 fighter jets to roughly 50,000 US service members already stationed in the region.
  • Brent crude jumped 4.5% to about $102.50 a barrel on reports of the buildup, with three tankers attacked in the Strait of Hormuz this week.

The United States is deploying a third aircraft carrier towards Iran, a US official told Al Jazeera, as the war enters its eighth month and Washington weighs whether to escalate. The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group departed its San Diego base on Sunday and is heading towards the region, followed a day later by the Makin Island Marine Expeditionary Force carrying more than 2,000 Marines.

By the end of November, three US aircraft carriers and two amphibious landing groups are expected to be positioned around Iran, the official said. The concentration of force would hand President Donald Trump a wider menu of military options if he decides to intensify operations. The latest deployment includes thousands of additional troops and air power, including F-35 fighter jets, layered on top of the roughly 50,000 US service members already stationed in the region.

Context & Background

The USS Theodore Roosevelt joins the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington already in the region, the latter having relieved the USS Abraham Lincoln in August after a record-setting deployment. The new deployment is expected to arrive between late October and November, according to US officials cited in multiple reports.

The buildup is intended to keep military options available to Trump regardless of how diplomatic efforts unfold. The Pentagon is reportedly not planning to withdraw any assets even if Washington and Tehran reach an agreement, and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has said American forces are "ready to go" if Trump orders further strikes.

Impact & Analysis

Energy markets reacted immediately: Brent futures jumped 4.5% to about $102.50 a barrel on Thursday after the Wall Street Journal first reported the deployment, with US West Texas Intermediate climbing 3% above $93 a barrel. The spike comes as crude flows from the Middle East have largely recovered to pre-war levels — a recovery that remains fragile, with at least three tankers attacked this week while transiting the Strait of Hormuz and Iran and its Houthi allies hitting regional refineries.

On the diplomatic front, the track suffered a blow after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio ordered Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his diplomatic mission to depart New York; Araghchi relocated to Doha, where Qatari envoys continue mediation efforts. The US Treasury this week also imposed sanctions on Iranian rail and automotive conglomerates, aimed at cutting off remaining sources of revenue for Tehran.

Diaspora Angle

With millions of Indians working across the Gulf, any disruption to shipping lanes or energy supplies hits home directly — oil above $100 feeds straight into Indian fuel prices and remittance corridors, making this buildup one to watch for families dependent on the region.

What's Next

All eyes are on November. Trump has told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran after the midterm elections, according to the Wall Street Journal, and has publicly said he believes the US would "win the war" with Iran "very soon" — though he has also suggested he would prefer not to discuss the details ahead of the vote.
